REG_SRG_002: The EDA Company Profile service did not evaluate the credentials: the session call answered 503 and said "EDA Company Profile API unreachable". A refusal caused by an outage says nothing about whether an unrecognised identifier is rejected, so this is blocked on infrastructure rather than passed. Re-run when the upstream is back.
REG_SRG_003: Passed 2026-09-09, and it is the case that defines what this feature is. The company name, address, licence and tax number are rendered from the EDA Company Profile above the note "From EDA Company Profile - read only", and every one of them is genuinely non-editable. So the company that gets registered is decided by the credentials, not by anything typed on the form - there is no field in which to name a different company. EPTTS_EDA_PROFILE_ID=user-152 resolves to "Marcyrl pharmaceuticals industries - MPI", licence 62814, tax 205131794. Where EDA holds no value the field explains itself rather than offering a blank box.
REG_SRG_004: Passed 2026-09-09. A 12-digit GLN and a 13-character GLN containing a letter are both refused with "GLN must be exactly 13 digits.", and nothing is transmitted - validation is client-side and PUT /onboarding/registration/company is only reached once every rule passes. NOTE the over-length case: #tnt-gln carries maxlength=13, so 14 digits cannot be typed - it truncates to a VALID GLN and validation moves on. The first draft of this case asserted a length complaint for it and failed against correct behaviour; it now asserts the field cannot hold more than 13 characters instead. The check digit is NOT validated at this step (the rule is /^\d{13}$/); that is left to the GS1 registry check.
REG_SRG_005: Passed 2026-09-09. A 3-digit GCP, one containing a letter and an empty one are all refused naming the GCP, and the field will not hold more than 12 characters. The GLN is satisfied first with a real check-digit-valid value, because the handler stops at the first failure and a blank GLN would have produced a GLN complaint instead.
REG_SRG_006: Passed 2026-09-09. National IDs of 13 digits, 7 digits and 14 characters including a letter are each refused with "National ID Number must be exactly 14 digits." - not the generic required-field message, which matters because the applicant HAS supplied a value. Every earlier rule is satisfied first so the refusal can only concern the national ID. The check digit and the encoded birth date are not validated; the platform rule is length only.
REG_SRG_009: Blocked on test data, not on a defect. Missing: EPTTS_SRG_GLN, EPTTS_SRG_GCP, EPTTS_SRG_GOVERNORATE, EPTTS_SRG_DISTRICT, EPTTS_SRG_FP_NAME_EN, EPTTS_SRG_FP_NAME_AR, EPTTS_SRG_FP_EMAIL, EPTTS_SRG_FP_PHONE, EPTTS_SRG_FP_NID, EPTTS_SRG_FP_NID_EXPIRY, EPTTS_SRG_FP_TITLE_EN, EPTTS_SRG_FP_TITLE_AR. This case advances a real registration on a registry with no delete control, so it cannot invent its inputs: the GLN/GCP must be registered to the logged-in company in the GS1 registry, and the focal point's national ID is a real person's identity document. Set these in automation-hub/.env once the applicant has supplied them.
